title: This Site

summary.title: My Resume Website - Summary
summary.content: This website, my all new resume website, showcases a large portion of crucial web development and programming skills I have been working on over the past several years. The biggest change in this website is that it has been built from the ground up using Angular, and Material Angular. In the past, I have used React, along with a combination of other tools to build my fullstack websites, but I have moved to Angular as a personal preference to the opinionated framework, making it easier for me to create full fledged web apps from the ground up without chasing down extra libraries. This project includes an Angular front end, hosted on GCP with an ExpressJS server, which also connects to a FireStore database for the contact page.

challenges: This project has presented two major challenges for me, both of which have given me crucial growth as a developer. One: bundle size, and Two: styling. The former has been a focus point on making sure that despite only being deployed on one central US server, my site can be quickly loaded from anywhere within the US. I tackled this challenge through a combination of lazy loaded routes, lazy loaded images, and utilization of special build features like tree shaking. For styling, I wanted to make sure this website would be visually appealing as well as functional. The main things I added to make this site pop are animations on initial load, and full-width title banners incorporating gradients for pages.

title: Interpreters

summary.title: Interpreters - Summary
summary.content: For the past 6 months, I have begun a new journey to creating compilers and interpreters. This fascination started when I looked into ways to contribute to the various tools I use in programming on a daily basis, and decided that language hacking would be a good suit for me. I therefore bought the fantastic book called Crafting Interpreters and began my studies. I have since learned several aspects of language creation, such as how to implement scoping, environments, variable interning, call frames, garbage collection, and so much more. This has truly elevated my understanding of programming in ways I could not imagine, and I am truly looking forward to contributing to languages in the near future. While Lox, the toy language I created directly from the book, is implemented in Java (tree walker) and C (Pratt compiler) separately, I am now reimplementing the language in C++ which will compile an AST to bytecode, and include several modern language features like compound assignment, arrays, lambdas, computed variables, break and continue statements, and more.

challenges: Needless to say, implementing even these toy languages presented several challenges and opportunities to grow as a programmer, especially in the realm of data structures. Implementing these languages required creating a hash table from scratch in c, something I hadn’t previously done, and which greatly improved my understanding of the structure. Additionally, the garbage collector used graph traversal methods for clean up, specifically a tri-colored graph, which presented several challenges but ultimately helped me further understand that data structure. This is also what brought me into design patterns with the visitor pattern, and allowed me to think much more abstractly about programming problems and their solutions after carefully studying, tracing, and understanding several types of design patterns and how they can better my code.

title: C++

summary.title: C++ - Summary
summary.content: This project is nothing more than a simple repository I used for learning the fundamentals of C++, as well as design patterns in OOP. This project includes all of the fundamentals through semi advanced concepts in C++, and helped me learn a lot about the C++ programming language, such as the behind the scenes of classes with multi-class inheritance, vtables, preparser techniques, pointer algorithm, and memory management. Additionally, this repository contains several of the most fundamental design pattern principles of OOP, further expanding my knowledge and thought  process for programming. Finally, there is also a subdirectory dedicated to the C++ standard library, going through concurrency with threads, thread pools, futures, atomics and mutexes; as well as containers, IO, Smart Pointers, and other general utilities.

challenges: The challenges in this project were all about making me think differently for a lower level language, specifically around pointers and memory management. Before C++, I really was clueless as to what stack or heap memory was, because it didn’t matter to me yet in other languages, and while I did a little bit of memory management in Swift, using weak and unowned variables, I didn’t have a full grasp as to what that truly meant. After going through C++, and painstakingly studying pointer algorithm and different memory structures, I now have a much more solid understanding of stack and heap memory, their benefits and drawbacks, pointers, how memory is traversed, pass-by rules, and so much more that not only enables me to take advantage of the full computer in lower level languages, but also gives me a much higher understanding of the higher level languages I use everyday.

title: Scrumdinger

summary.title: Scrumdinger - Summary
summary.content: Swift has been my wonderful introduction to the world of native app development, and the Scrumdinger tutorial app showcases several of the most important parts of developing both a mobile app in general, and mobile apps for Apple. This app uses a combination of SwiftUI, SwiftData, Foundation, CoreAudio, and other Apple development frameworks to make a full scale production application. This app features several navigation destinations, as well as persistent data, using SwiftData and SQLite, and follows accessibility guidelines, making the user experience for all users. Additionally, in similar tutorial native Apple apps, I have gone through the process of writing unit test code, ensuring successful production, as well as turning apps cross platform, and reusing a large majority of business logic across platforms, while tailoring viewing experiences to each device.

challenges: The two main challenges I faced in this project were learning how to effectively store persistent data and learn about the object graph used by the Apple ecosystem to increase app performance, as well as further learning concurrency models and intros to grand central dispatch, to enable truly performant code. While not all of this is directly showcased in this project, future projects to be posted will incorporate several of the key factors learned through this project.

title: MUI

summary.title: MUI - Summary
summary.content: Contributing to MUI was an incredibly important experience for me in my software engineering learning path. This gave me foundational knowledge on how to navigate and code in a large code repository, as well as utilizing version control on a large scale to properly write code. My PRs, adding loading to the base button, and reordering modal action for accessibility users, widened my view for development to not only code, but focus on performance, accessibility, teamwork, and unit testing. Overall, my experience contributing to the MUI open source project has prepared me for my next steps in open source, where I will be turning to either V8 or Swift for a long term, more challenging project, to focus on my goals of contributing to a programming language.

challenges: The challenges in this project were both about new coding practices, as well as soft skills. Not only was I challenged with incorporating new unit tests, as well as making sure I followed best practices for commits and version control, I was also introduced to working with a group of people in the open source community, where I learned to better communicate, ask question, and bring up new ideas.
